comparison: Both address claims C87-C92 about uniformity of terminal structures within arbor types and labeled line organization. OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED based on comprehensive morphological observations across 719 arbors. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting that LA-FACE arbors sometimes have free endings (possibly due to P21 developmental stage) and stating 'whether the morphological classification system used here really corresponds well to function remains to be seen.'

Both evaluate claims C93-C101 regarding correspondences between morphological and physiological classifications. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging they are speculative without direct physiological validation. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, noting the study 'relies on past descriptions' and 'whether the morphological classification system used here really corresponds well to function remains to be seen,' though they accept the morphological observations themselves.

Both address claims C137-C145 about advantages of the cutaneous system and C83 about being first systematic description. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, noting experimental and technical advantages are well-established. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, recognizing this as 'a significant original contribution' and explicitly valuing the methodology and quantitative assays, noting 'this was very difficult to appreciate from the kinds of morphological studies in prior papers.'

Both evaluate methodological claims. OpenEval R28 addresses C146-C171 (comprehensive methods) finding them SUPPORTED with good reproducibility. Peer R1 addresses overlapping claims C146-C171 plus genetic strategy claims C2-C6 and dataset claims C13-C21, finding them SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly recognize the 'inducible-intersectional genetic strategy' and 'morphometric and quantitative assays' as having 'general implications for many scientists.'

Both address claims C22-C26 about limitations of labeling strategy and C84-C86 about incompleteness of survey. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, noting appropriate scientific caution. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'these limitations are discussed frankly by the authors and are not an impediment to publication' and that 'the non-randomness is fully understood by the authors.'

OpenEval R1 addresses C1-C10 including validation that Brn3a+/- neurons are functionally normal (C7-C10), finding all SUPPORTED. Peer R2 specifically addresses C7-C10 but rates them UNCERTAIN, noting 'one issue not fully discussed is the fact that the neurons are hemizygous for Brn3a' and requesting more explicit discussion of potential subtle phenotypes despite acknowledging compensatory autoregulation.

Both address claims C127-C131 about developmental mechanisms and competition models. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the competition model is supported by analogy but remains speculative without experimental validation. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, requesting authors 'avoid diluting the information with speculation that may or may not be correct,' indicating these should be presented as hypotheses rather than supported conclusions.

OpenEval R26 addresses C134-C136 about follicle polarity transmission, rating UNCERTAIN due to reliance on unpublished observations. Peer R8 addresses C134-C136 plus other mechanistic claims (C127-C131, C133), rating all UNCERTAIN and requesting authors avoid speculation. Both agree these are hypotheses requiring validation.

OpenEval R25 addresses C132-C133 about morphological diversity and transcriptional control mechanisms, rating SUPPORTED for diversity observation but noting regulatory mechanisms are speculative. Peer R8 includes C133 among mechanistic claims rated UNCERTAIN, requesting authors avoid speculation that may not be correct.

OpenEval R19 addresses C102-C108 about receptive field predictions, rating SUPPORTED as well-reasoned and testable hypotheses. Peer R7 addresses C102-C108 plus other functional predictions (C109-C126), rating all UNCERTAIN and requesting authors 'strengthen the paper by focusing on a few clear conclusions and avoid diluting the information with speculation.'

OpenEval R20 addresses C109-C114 about directional sensitivity mechanism, rating UNCERTAIN as the structural asymmetry is well-documented but functional implications remain speculative. Peer R7 includes C109-C114 among functional predictions rated UNCERTAIN, requesting focus on clear conclusions rather than speculation.

OpenEval R21 addresses C115-C117 about LD-FALE functional role, rating UNCERTAIN as morphological observations are solid but functional assignment remains speculative. Peer R7 includes C115-C117 among functional predictions rated UNCERTAIN, requesting authors avoid speculation that may not be correct.

OpenEval R22 addresses C118-C120 about LA-FACE innervation patterns and multi-arbor convergence, rating SUPPORTED though noting inference would be strengthened by higher resolution imaging. Peer R7 includes C118-C120 among functional predictions rated UNCERTAIN, treating these as speculative hypotheses rather than established findings.

OpenEval R23 addresses C121-C126 about coverage factor estimates, rating UNCERTAIN as these involve assumptions requiring validation. Peer R7 includes C121-C126 among functional predictions rated UNCERTAIN, requesting authors avoid speculation and focus on clear conclusions.

OpenEval R2 addresses C11-C21 about experimental dataset and methodology, rating SUPPORTED with well-justified choices and clear documentation. Peer R1 includes C13-C21 (timing, dose-response, dataset size) among methodological claims rated SUPPORTED, explicitly recognizing the methodology as having general implications.

OpenEval R4 addresses C27-C29, C65-C66 about classification methodology, rating SUPPORTED. Peer R4 addresses these plus comprehensive morphological characterization claims C27-C82, C132, rating all SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the best support for the validity of the classification method is that the larger arbors seem to have predominantly a single kind of ending' and recognize this as 'a significant original contribution.'

OpenEval R5 addresses C30-C35 about small arbor morphologies with caveats, rating SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes C30-C35 among comprehensive morphological claims rated SUPPORTED, recognizing the quality of results and validity of classification method.

OpenEval R6 addresses C36-C38 about BE arbor morphometric characterization, rating SUPPORTED with quantitative reproducible measurements. Peer R4 includes C36-C38 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED, recognizing the quality of results.
OpenEval R7 addresses C39-C40 about TE arbor characterization, rating SUPPORTED with quantitative data. Peer R4 includes C39-C40 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R8 addresses C41-C43 about LD-FALE arbor characterization, rating SUPPORTED with quantitative data and documented anterior orientation. Peer R4 includes C41-C43 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R9 addresses C44-C50 about HD-FALE arbor characterization, rating SUPPORTED with comprehensive documentation. Peer R4 includes C44-C50 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R10 addresses C51-C52 about SA-FACE arbor characterization, rating SUPPORTED with quantitative data. Peer R4 includes C51-C52 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R11 addresses C53-C56 about LA-FACE arbor characterization, rating SUPPORTED including inverse relationship between arbor size and follicle density. Peer R4 includes C53-C56 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R12 addresses C57-C64 about LA-FE arbor characterization, rating SUPPORTED with remarkable axon lengths well-documented. Peer R4 includes C57-C64 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R13 addresses C67-C72 about quantitative morphometric relationships, rating SUPPORTED with clear demonstrations. Peer R4 includes C67-C72 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R14 addresses C73-C77 about quantitative distinctions between morphologically similar arbor pairs, rating SUPPORTED with sophisticated morphometric analysis. Peer R4 includes C73-C77 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R15 addresses C78-C82 about laminar organization, rating SUPPORTED with quantitative depth measurements. Peer R4 includes C78-C82 among morphological claims rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R16 addresses C83-C86 about contribution and limitations, rating SUPPORTED with appropriate scientific caution. Peer R3 includes C84-C86 (but not C83) among limitation claims rated SUPPORTED, stating limitations are 'discussed frankly' and 'not an impediment to publication.'

OpenEval R1 addresses C1-C10 including genetic construct design C2-C6, rating all SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C2-C6 among methodological claims rated SUPPORTED, explicitly recognizing the 'inducible-intersectional genetic strategy' as having general implications.
